title: Converged Hosted Endpoints PRD: Unified Chat/Completions/Embeddings/Rerank (Phase 1)
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Phase 1 PRD to deliver a converged, production-ready set of hosted endpoints for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank. This PRD defines the API contract for v1, non-functional requirements (latency, availability, cost targets), acceptance criteria, and the launch checklist for self-serve availability.
background: Customers have asked for consistent behavior and observability across text generation and retrieval primitives. Currently our hosted endpoints have diverging params and quality controls. This initiative unifies core concepts (prompt/inputs, response streaming, token accounting, error codes, rate limiting) and adds an explicit rerank endpoint to support retrieval-augmented workflows.
goals: Deliver a single, well-documented hosted API surface for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank that is intuitive for engineers
Meet production SLOs: P50 latency < 120ms for small completions, P95 < 500ms for chat streaming token continuations where feasible
Provide clear acceptance criteria and automated tests to prevent regressions in quality and cost
Ship SDK updates and migration guides so customers can move from legacy endpoints with minimal friction
Support staged rollout (canary -> gradual) and full observability in Redwood Console
non_goals: Model training, fine-tuning or hosting private customer models in this phase
Large redesign of billing model; we'll carry forward existing per-token usage billing with clearer reporting
Feature parity with every legacy experimental flag—focus on common paths first
scope_included: Streaming responses for chat and long completions via SSE/HTTP streams
Clear, documented error codes and retry semantics
SDK updates (Javascript, Python) with helper types and examples
Console dashboards for per-endpoint latency, token cost, error rates and model fallback events
Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback thresholds
scope_excluded: Dedicated capacity and Private (VPC) deployment changes in this release—those will follow in Dedicated/Private tracks
Large B2B onboarding support for enterprise-only rate limit exemptions
New quantization/compile profile tuning for inference kernels
requirements: Req-1: Each endpoint must accept standardized request envelopes with top-level fields: input(s), model, temperature/decoding params, max_tokens, and optional metadata headers
Req-2: Streaming must support chunked token events and a final terminal event; partial response tokens must include incremental usage estimates
Req-3: Embeddings endpoint must return deterministic vector length per model, L2-normalized when requested
Req-4: Rerank endpoint must accept a query and a list of candidate documents and return a scored ranking with confidence scores and a stable sorting tie-breaker
Req-5: Backwards-compatible headers: X-Redwood-Request-Id must be present in responses for traceability
Req-6: Rate limiting and quotas must be per-account with 429 semantics and Retry-After header
Req-7: Error taxonomy must distinguish client (4xx), model-limited (409/429), transient server (5xx), and policy violations (403)
api_contract_summary: Chat (/v1/chat) - supports messages array, role tags, function calling metadata, streaming; default model alias 'redwood/chat-default'
Completions (/v1/completions) - broad generation endpoint for single prompt; supports n, stop sequences, best_of; streaming optional
Embeddings (/v1/embeddings) - accepts input string(s) or batches; response contains embeddings array and model id; supports batch_size param
Rerank (/v1/rerank) - accepts query and candidates; response returns candidate IDs with score and normalized_score; supports batching and per-candidate metadata
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: End-to-end functional tests pass for all endpoints in preprod with canonical prompt/embedding/rerank suites
AC-2: Load test: sustained throughput of X qps for small chat requests with < 1% errors at target SLOs (define X with ENG load test results)
AC-3: SDKs (JS/Python) publish passing integration tests that call staging endpoints and verify responses and streaming behavior
AC-4: Console shows per-route breakdown and the new token-level cost view; sample dashboard created in Console templates
AC-5: Migration guide published with at least two code examples per SDK and clear deprecation notes for legacy endpoints
AC-6: Security review completed and SSO/KMS considerations documented; no open critical issues
AC-7: Canary rollout executed with 5% traffic for 24 hours, metrics within rollback thresholds (error rate < 0.5% above baseline, latency P95 not > 2x baseline)
launch_checklist: Docs: Finalized API reference pages for each endpoint and streaming guide
SDKs: Release JS v3.1.0 and Python v2.9.0 with migration helpers
Billing: Validate token accounting and confirm per-token reporting appears in customer Consoles
Monitoring: Dashboards for latency, errors, token usage, and model fallback configured and alerted
Security: Completed security review and infra checklist; secrets rotation and KMS integration smoke-tested
Compliance: Legal sign-off on terms and privacy updates for hosted usage
Support: Runbook and playbook drafted for common incidents and assigned on-call rotation
Release notes and migration guide published in Docs and linked from Console
Canary: Start at 5% with automated rollback configured and run for 24 hours
Post-launch: 7-day incident hunting schedule and weekly metrics review set up
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha - dev & infra teams only; smoke tests and load calibrations
Phase 1: Canary - 5% of traffic from non-enterprise orgs for 24h; monitor rollback thresholds
Phase 2: Gradual - 25% for 48h, then 50% for 72h if stable
Phase 3: General availability - automatic migration flag for new signups and opt-in migration guides for existing customers
monitoring_and_slo: SLO-1: Availability 99.95% per-week for v1 endpoints
SLO-2: Latency targets - chat small P50 < 120ms, chat token generation P95 < 500ms where streaming cannot be avoided
SLO-3: Error budget alerts tied to 4xx/5xx spike detection and model fallback frequency
Metric list: p50/p95 latency, qps, error rate by status code, tokens_generated per_request, costs_per_token estimate, model_fallback_count
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Streaming regressions could disrupt client UX. Mitigation: provide non-stream fallback, tighten integration tests, include streaming smoke-tests in CI
Risk: Unexpected token accounting mismatch with billing pipeline. Mitigation: reconcile token counts in staging against billing and add end-to-end token tests
Risk: Rerank scoring divergence from customers' expectations. Mitigation: include calibration dataset, expose explainability fields (top contributing features) where possible
Risk: High peak load could breach latency SLO. Mitigation: autoscaling safeguards and model fallback to cheaper variants under load

decisions: Decision: Use a unified top-level request envelope for all four endpoints to simplify SDKs and telemetry
Decision: Maintain existing billing model for Phase 1 but surface per-token cost in Console for transparency
Decision: Rerank returns normalized_score in [0,1] and raw_score for internal debugging only
qa_plan: Unit tests for request envelope validation and response shapes
Integration tests hitting preprod models simulating chat, completion, embedding, rerank flows
Streaming stability tests with network partitioning and reconnection scenarios
Load tests with gradual ramp and soak phases; verify billing telemetry during soak
